review_candidates.title: Customer Success Manager
review_candidates.description: Help customers turn a promising product into a useful habit. Forcivate builds AI products, including Friday Force, an AI-driven marketing platform. We need a Customer Success Manager who helps customers connect the product to real business goals, build confidence using it, and keep making progress after their first walkthrough. You will own the customer’s operational success relationship: understanding desired outcomes, guiding onboarding, encouraging useful adoption, and responding early when progress stalls. This is a hands-on opportunity to shape how customer success works as well as deliver it. Your judgment should help customers succeed today and make tomorrow’s customer experience easier to deliver. What you will own Discover each customer’s goals, starting point, stakeholders, and constraints. Turn that understanding into a short success plan with an agreed first-value milestone, next actions, and clear responsibilities. Lead onboarding, training, and product walkthroughs. Adapt your explanation to the customer’s confidence and workflow, and verify they can complete meaningful tasks independently after the session. Monitor activation and usage alongside customer conversations. Identify stalled onboarding, declining engagement, and unmet expectations; prioritize proactive outreach by likely impact rather than contacting everyone identically. Manage practical recovery plans for at-risk customers. Listen carefully, distinguish product friction from expectation or workflow gaps, agree next steps, and keep the customer informed without promising unapproved fixes. Handle initial support questions within agreed coverage and coordinate issues requiring specialists. Capture reproducible steps, expected and actual behavior, and relevant context; track resolution without being expected to code fixes. Keep accurate customer records, health assessments, commitments, and follow-up dates. Build reusable onboarding guidance and answers that reduce repeated friction while preserving a personal customer relationship. Give Product and Engineering actionable feedback, separating individual requests from recurring patterns. Bring evidence of customer impact and help verify whether a shipped improvement addresses the original problem. Partner with the Account Executive on renewal readiness, expansion signals, and relevant post-sale demos. Remain the operational owner while the AE handles commercial discussions and proposed renewal negotiation. What you bring Demonstrated ownership of SaaS customers, with specific examples of improving onboarding, adoption, customer confidence, or retention; explain your contribution and the evidence behind the result. Clear professional English for US customer conversations and written follow-up. You can listen, explain a workflow simply, and handle a difficult conversation with empathy and precision. Structured problem-solving: you investigate friction, test your understanding, document useful details, and know when and how to escalate. Reliable organization across multiple accounts, including accurate records, explicit commitments, and timely follow-through. Initiative and learning speed: you can learn a changing product, prioritize competing needs, and improve a process without waiting for a complete playbook. Helpful, not required: familiarity with marketing workflows; experience in an early-stage SaaS business; creating training materials or lightweight customer-health processes. Your first 90 days In the first 30 days, learn the product and customer journeys, agree what onboarding completion and first value mean, and establish a usable account and risk view. By day 60, independently run onboarding and outreach, document completion and time-to-value evidence, and maintain recovery plans with owners and next steps. By day 90, show how those actions affected adoption and customer progress, identify recurring friction, and recommend the next improvements. Renewal and retention outcomes will be reviewed where enough time and customer volume exist; activity counts alone will not define success. How we work and apply Expect high ownership, fast iteration, direct feedback, customer empathy, and accountability. Proactive success and initial reactive support share this role; priorities and coverage will be agreed, with specialist escalation available through the team. You will help build repeatable systems, not simply manage a queue.

review_candidates.title: Senior Software Engineer, Backend (Infrastructure)
review_candidates.description: About Nutrient At Nutrient, we're revolutionizing how the world works with documents. Our tools transform static files into intelligent, secure workflows, empowering businesses to innovate faster and smarter. Trusted by thousands of organizations across 80 countries, including Fortune 500 companies and public sector leaders, our platform supports nearly a billion end users globally in industries where documents aren't just files, they're mission-critical. Your Role at Nutrient... We’re looking for a backend engineer passionate about building robust and scalable systems, excited about working with modern cloud technologies and distributed systems to power our Document Engine and SaaS products. You find satisfaction in architecting high-performance solutions, optimising system reliability, caring for the cloud infrastructure our products run on, and creating efficient backend services that handle complex document processing workflows at scale. You work in an AI-native way: you hand research and implementation work to agents, review their output critically, and build tooling that makes you and the team faster. What You'll Work On... Execute on the design and implementation of high-performance Elixir/Phoenix-based systems such as Nutrient's Document Engine and Web Services API Design and build declarative infrastructure, robust, scalable and easy to observe and maintain (we are currently using Terraform, Terramate and FluxCD on Kubernetes, with Helm charts powering both our managed cloud and customer self-hosted deployments) Operate and evolve our managed cloud platform: cluster lifecycle and upgrades, GitOps workflows, observability, and database operations, keeping it reliable, secure, and costefficient Share ownership for architecture, tools and services, contribute to product development and customer success Collaborate closely with a small, remote-first engineering team to ship features, debug hard problems, and continuously improve reliability Build systems and workflows that use AI to speed up our work, from agent-driven investigation of performance issues to automating repetitive engineering tasks Meet in person with the team periodically to align and reflect What You'll Bring... Experience in backend services and distributed systems A track record running production workloads on Kubernetes and public cloud (we use AWS), ideally with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps practices Strong coding skills: Elixir experience isn't required, we'll help you learn You work AI-native: agents are part of how you research, investigate and ship code, and you stay fully accountable for what goes out A pragmatic approach to code: you appreciate clean architecture but know when good enough is the right call A culture of direct feedback: you speak up when something isn't right and take feedback just as well Who Thrives Here... At Nutrient, we’re not just hiring for skills — we’re hiring for mindset. The people who thrive here are: Collaborators: You collaborate openly, listen actively, and prioritize team success over ego. Hungry Learners: Rapid learning fuels progress and career growth. Curious Thinkers: You dig deep to uncover the “why,” valuing understanding over simply being right. Self-Starters: You take action without waiting for direction, turning obstacles into opportunities with creativity and persistence. Owners: You take responsibility for solutions and outcomes, always looking for ways to improve what’s within your control. Doers: You’re energized by progress, motivated to create meaningful impact, and eager to tackle challenges. Why You'll Love Working Here... At Nutrient, we build tools that reshape how businesses and developers work with documents. Our culture is centred on continuous growth and collaboration. Every team member has room to learn, innovate, and drive meaningful impact. Real platform ownership: You’ll help run and evolve the managed cloud behind Document Engine (cluster lifecycle, GitOps, and observability), not just ship services on top of it. Modern stack end to end: Elixir and Phoenix for the product, Kubernetes with Terraform, Helm, and FluxCD for the infrastructure it runs on. Fully remote and async-first: Minimal meetings, strong writing culture, and the independence to manage your own work. Mission-critical product: Nutrient's platform is trusted by 15%+ of the Global 500 across 80+ countries. Strong growth trajectory: ARR grown from $28M to $49M over the past two years, backed by Insight Partners, with a $100M+ investment fuelling further growth. Nutrient believes in equal opportunity. We employ people from many cultures and countries, celebrate diversity, and are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, skill sets, and perspectives. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, age, marital status, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other non-merit factor.
